newsitem.title: USA: D&P downgrades Darden debt to triple-B-plus.
newsitem.headline: D&P downgrades Darden debt to triple-B-plus.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said on Friday that it downgraded its rating on Darden Restaurants Inc senior unsecured debt to triple-B-plus from single-A-minus.
The longer term rating applies to about $250 million of outstanding notes and debentures.

The rating action is primarily due to current unprecedented earnings volatility at its premier restaurant concept, Red Lobster, coupled with management's decision to expand the company's share repurchase program, D&P said in a statement.

D&P also said it lowered the rating on Darden's commercial paper to D-2 from D-1 and assigned a preliminary rating of triple-B-plus to any senior debt issued from the $250 million remaining under Darden's outstanding debt shelf registration.

Disappointing sales and operating profit results at Red Lobster signal a loss of momentum at the concept, D&P said. Management has taken several steps to reverse the decline but a turnaround at Red Lobster will take time, it said. Consequently, operating results for Darden are expected to be depressed for the current fiscal year. Furthermore, a return to former levels of profitability is by no means assured, D&P said.
Darden's strengths include is strong brand name for both Red Lobster and Olive Garden restaurant concepts, D&P added.
Darden shares were trading unchanged at 8-1/2.
